title_en: Bank of China, Zhujiang Branch v. Traditional Investment Co., Ltd. of Hong Kong et al. — dispute over guarantee contract
keywords_en: civil; dispute over guarantee contract; first instance; intermediate people's court; Guangdong Province; legal person; state organ; Civil Procedure Law; jurisdictional objection; suretyship liability; re-guarantee obligation; validity of mortgage; partial support; loan guarantee; debt subrogation; equity transfer; mortgaged property; contract dispute; guarantee; suretyship; mortgage; jurisdiction; dispute over guarantee contract involving a capital limited company and others
full_text_en:
Bank of China Zhujiang Branch v. Hong Kong Traditional Investment Co., Ltd., et al. — Dispute over Guarantee Contract

Plaintiff: Bank of China Zhujiang Branch.
Legal representative: Liu Dengtang, President.

Defendant: Hong Kong Traditional Investment Co., Ltd.
Legal representative: Shi Meixuan, Chairman.

Defendant: Guangzhou Haizhu District Foreign Economic Relations and Trade Commission, Guangdong Province.
Legal representative: Liang Rongsen, Director.

Defendant: Guangzhou Jiangnan Hotel Co., Ltd., Guangdong Province.
Legal representative: Ou Zhunming, Chairman.

The plaintiff, Bank of China Zhujiang Branch (hereinafter referred to as "Zhujiang Bank"), filed a lawsuit with the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court, Guangdong Province, against the defendants, Hong Kong Traditional Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Traditional Company"), Guangzhou Haizhu District Foreign Economic Relations and Trade Commission, Guangdong Province (hereinafter referred to as "District Foreign Economic Commission"), and Guangzhou Jiangnan Hotel Co., Ltd., Guangdong Province (hereinafter referred to as "Jiangnan Company"), regarding a dispute over a guarantee contract. The plaintiff, Zhujiang Bank, alleged: The defendant Traditional Company borrowed HKD 79,170,000 from Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation (hereinafter referred to as "HSBC"). The plaintiff acted as the guarantor for this loan. After the repayment period expired, Traditional Company failed to repay as agreed. In response, the plaintiff, as the guarantor, repaid the entire amount on its behalf. The plaintiff now requests the court to order Traditional Company to repay the plaintiff, or to satisfy the debt with the property jointly mortgaged to the plaintiff by Traditional Company and the defendant Jiangnan Company, and to order the defendant District Foreign Economic Commission to assume the obligation of a sub-guarantor for the debt owed by Traditional Company to the plaintiff.

The defendant Traditional Company argued: The plaintiff Zhujiang Bank and HSBC had previously entered into a guarantee agreement regarding the defendant's loan. That agreement stipulated that in the event of a dispute, English law would apply and the English courts would have jurisdiction. Therefore, the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court has no jurisdiction over this case and should dismiss the plaintiff's complaint.

The defendant Jiangnan Company argued: Zhujiang Bank's lawsuit against this company does not comply with the provisions of Article 108 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and requests dismissal of the complaint.

The defendant District Foreign Economic Commission argued: The facts alleged by the plaintiff Zhujiang Bank have no direct legal relationship with this Commission, and this Commission should not be named as a defendant.

After reviewing the jurisdictional objection raised by the defendant Traditional Company, the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court held: Pursuant to the "Agreement on Fulfilling Guarantee Obligations" entered into between Zhujiang Bank and Traditional Company, when Traditional Company was unable to repay the loan to HSBC as agreed, Zhujiang Bank repaid the loan to HSBC on behalf of Traditional Company as stipulated. Subsequently, Traditional Company failed to repay the compensation amount to Zhujiang Bank within the agreed period. Zhujiang Bank has the right to demand Traditional Company to fulfill its repayment obligation, thereby creating a new creditor-debtor relationship between Zhujiang Bank and Traditional Company. This is a separate legal relationship from the guarantee provided by Zhujiang Bank to HSBC for Traditional Company's loan. Moreover, the "Agreement on Fulfilling Guarantee Obligations" between Zhujiang Bank and Traditional Company was signed in Guangzhou, China. Pursuant to Article 243 of the Civil Procedure Law, this court has jurisdiction over disputes arising from the performance of this agreement. Traditional Company's argument that Zhujiang Bank and HSBC had mutually agreed on jurisdiction and that this court has no jurisdiction over this case is untenable. In its complaint, Zhujiang Bank requested that Jiangnan Company execute the "House Mortgage Agreement" signed between the parties if Traditional Company fails to repay the compensation amount as agreed. Therefore, Jiangnan Company should be a defendant in this case. The District Foreign Economic Commission had issued a sub-guarantee letter to Zhujiang Bank; until it fully performs its guarantee obligations to the plaintiff, it should participate in this lawsuit as a party. Accordingly, the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court ruled to dismiss Traditional Company's jurisdictional objection. Traditional Company appealed. The Guangdong High People's Court, after trial, ruled to dismiss Traditional Company's appeal and affirmed the jurisdictional ruling of the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court, through public trial, found the following facts: Lianxing Agricultural, Industrial and Commercial Corporation of Xinjiao (pronounced jiào) Town, Haizhu District, Guangzhou (hereinafter referred to as "Lianxing Company") constructed the Guangzhou Jiangnan Hotel. Due to insufficient funds after opening, it entered into a cooperative operation agreement with the defendant Traditional Company. The contract stipulated: Traditional Company would invest USD 14.5 million, holding 55% equity, and Lianxing Company would invest USD 10 million, holding 45% equity, to jointly establish Jiangnan Company for the cooperative operation of Jiangnan Hotel. To raise funds, Traditional Company intended to borrow from HSBC and needed the plaintiff Zhujiang Bank to act as guarantor for its loan. To facilitate this, on April 2, 1987, Traditional Company, Lianxing Company, and Jiangnan Company entered into a four-party agreement with Zhujiang Bank, stipulating that the property and ancillary facilities of Jiangnan Hotel would be mortgaged to Zhujiang Bank, and Jiangnan Company would pay a guarantee fee to Zhujiang Bank at 1.2% of the total loan amount. The defendant District Foreign Economic Commission also issued a sub-guarantee letter to Zhujiang Bank, undertaking a sub-guarantee obligation for Zhujiang Bank's guarantee of Traditional Company's loan. Accordingly, Zhujiang Bank issued a letter of guarantee to HSBC, guaranteeing that Traditional Company would repay the loan on time. Traditional Company then borrowed HKD 79,170,000 from HSBC, all of which was invested in Jiangnan Company. Due to Jiangnan Company's operating losses, Traditional Company failed to repay the loan principal and interest to HSBC as agreed, and Jiangnan Company was unable to pay the guarantee fee to Zhujiang Bank. To fulfill its obligation as guarantor, Zhujiang Bank, in 1990, advanced HKD 10,188,500 to HSBC on behalf of Traditional Company, and on October 24, 1991, advanced the remaining full principal and interest of HKD 83,440,384.45. Thus, Zhujiang Bank advanced a total of HKD 93,628,884.45 in principal and interest for Traditional Company's loan. Zhujiang Bank obtained the certificates of beneficial rights that Traditional Company had mortgaged to HSBC at the time of borrowing, and paid HKD 52,733.30 in attorney fees, telephone charges, etc., for the transfer of such rights, and also paid other expenses of RMB 50,150 in fulfilling the guarantee obligations.

After Zhujiang Bank made the first advance payment for Traditional Company, the defendant District Foreign Economic Commission, in order to fulfill its sub-guarantee obligation, advanced HKD 3,118,000 to Zhujiang Bank on behalf of Traditional Company. This amount was transferred by Zhujiang Bank to HSBC to offset Traditional Company's loan.

The defendant Jiangnan Company, being unable to pay the 1990 guarantee fee of HKD 1,862,664 to Zhujiang Bank as agreed, had this amount converted by Zhujiang Bank into a loan to the company. However, Jiangnan Company still failed to pay the principal of this loan, the 1991 loan interest of HKD 201,458.68, and the 1991 guarantee fee of HKD 874,962.

During the trial, upon the application of the plaintiff Zhujiang Bank, the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court sealed up the property and ancillary facilities of Jiangnan Hotel and froze the proceeds due to Traditional Company from Jiangnan Company. To pay off its debts, Traditional Company proposed to transfer its equity in Jiangnan Company to Hong Kong Hong-Ao Holdings Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Holdings Company"). This action was consented to by Lianxing Company, but Zhujiang Bank objected on the grounds that Jiangnan Hotel was already the mortgaged property provided by Traditional Company and the owner had no right to transfer it before the debt was cleared. At the same time, Zhujiang Bank expressed its willingness to acquire Jiangnan Hotel on the same terms to offset Traditional Company's debt.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court held: The plaintiff Zhujiang Bank fulfilled its guarantee obligation for the defendant Traditional Company. Traditional Company should repay the loan principal and interest advanced by Zhujiang Bank as agreed and compensate the guarantor for losses suffered due to the fulfillment of the guarantee obligation. The defendant Jiangnan Company should fulfill its obligation to pay the guarantee fee as agreed. The defendant District Foreign Economic Commission should fulfill its sub-guarantee obligation as agreed. Currently, Traditional Company proposes to transfer its equity interest in Jiangnan Company to Holdings Company. This action is not only conducive to Traditional Company's repayment of debts but also takes into account the cooperative operation mode of Jiangnan Hotel, benefiting the future interests of all cooperative parties. Since Traditional Company's debt has not yet been cleared, after the transfer of its equity and until the debt is satisfied, the mortgage right of Zhujiang Bank over the property of Jiangnan Hotel should remain valid. Pursuant to Article 85 of the Civil Procedure Law, the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court presided over mediation between the parties. All parties, acting on a voluntary basis, reached the following agreement on May 11, 1992:

1. Within 12 months after the agreement to transfer equity to Holdings Company is approved and takes effect by the relevant authorities, Traditional Company shall repay the debt of HKD 93,628,884.45 to Zhujiang Bank.

2. The interest accrued on Traditional Company's debt of HKD 93,628,884.45 before the approval and effectiveness of the equity transfer agreement shall be repaid by Jiangnan Company to Zhujiang Bank on behalf of Traditional Company within 7 days from the date the agreement is approved and takes effect.

3. Jiangnan Company shall pay to Zhujiang Bank the 1991 guarantee fee of HKD 874,962 due as agreed, and the principal of HKD 1,862,664 converted from the 1990 guarantee fee into a loan, together with interest on that amount up to the date of payment, before the end of September 1992.

4. The other expenses of RMB 50,150 paid by Zhujiang Bank due to its assumption of guarantee responsibility shall be paid by Jiangnan Company to Zhujiang Bank on behalf of Traditional Company within 10 days from the effective date of this mediation statement.

5. If Traditional Company or Jiangnan Company fails to perform any of the obligations in items 1 to 4 of this mediation statement when due, Zhujiang Bank shall have the right to request the sealing up of the property, facilities, and other assets of Jiangnan Hotel and to have them sold to satisfy the debt.

6. After Zhujiang Bank recovers all amounts under items 1 to 4 of this mediation statement, it shall return to Traditional Company the certificates of beneficial rights of Traditional Company obtained from HSBC.

7. Traditional Company shall repay the amounts advanced on its behalf by Jiangnan Company and the District Foreign Economic Commission. The specific repayment method shall be separately agreed upon by the three parties.

The case acceptance fee is RMB 351,795, of which Zhujiang Bank shall bear 20% and Traditional Company shall bear 80%. The property preservation fee is RMB 318,786, which shall be borne by Traditional Company.
